page: Amazon Web Services r8g.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by 96 dedicated physical cores of the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 ARM64 architecture. Operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz, each core features a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, providing dedicated compute resources without simultaneous multithreading. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory, yielding a high density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It features a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps and does not include local storage or GPU hardware.

Benchmark data highlights the server's strong memory subsystem and multi-core capabilities. The r8g.metal-24xl achieves top-tier performance in multi-core processing, memory bandwidth (both cached small-block and uncached large-block reads and writes), and PassMark memory tests. Database operations and Redis SET operations also rank in the top tier, processing 198.34 million operations per second. However, single-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench remains in the average tier. Additionally, while medium and large LLM text generation speeds are strong, small model text generation falls into the bottom tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal architecture and high memory-to-core ratio make this server highly resource-dense for memory-bound workloads. The lack of bundled local storage means storage requirements must be handled externally, which represents a tradeoff for database deployments. This server is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, high-throughput web serving, and memory-intensive multi-threaded applications.
